answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card, adding one per fatigue and one more for Chairman. Modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the member to Pensioners, flips the card to Vacant Offices, and returns its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no normal office attrition roll.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: “Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.”

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card. Order is descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Do not replace cards during selection; if display empties, skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown). Return all unused Pensioners to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: “Players who retired at least one pensioner”; “descending actual total retirement spending”; “discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three.”

answers.answer: At Family phase start check whether the opportunity marker matched the action to be chosen; that permits taking that main action twice. Move marker to the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; it is not doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and a marker already on Enlist Writer, take Enlist Writer twice: each action places one writer plus one additional writer once this turn for having at least four vacant offices, for three writers total.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family: “may take it twice if the marker already matched it”; “extra action is never doubled”; Enlist Writer: “place one additional writer once this turn.”

answers.answer: After family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Initial share-purchase payments went to the bank, not Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family: “move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one”; Seek Share: “pay bank.”

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on card backs. Own-family hire requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool (except Chairman elections and Commander appointments). Promotion transfers fatigue to the new card and inserts the old vacant card into hiring order. If no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip it; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: “ascending number”; “verbal consent from every other player”; “transfer its fatigue”; “If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office.”

answers.answer: Former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Any shareholder can campaign; first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of winner’s shares into Chairman slot and give title. If no candidate reaches it, former Chairman chooses any shareholder including self. No Nepotism consent applies. The Chairman piece remains a Company share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.
answers.evidence: Hiring → Chairman election: “more than half of current shares”; “If no candidate gets support”; “still counts as a share… but cannot be traded or invested.”

answers.answer: Pay all check cash from the acting office’s own treasury to the bank before rolling. Gather dice and subtract penalties; lowest die governs: 1–2 success, 3–4 failure (retry if resources and office limits permit), 5–6 catastrophe: no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue, and flip card into Vacant Offices. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success (examples: trade with no ship, or deploy without dice just to risk officer losses).
answers.evidence: Company Operation → Success checks: “all cash…from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank”; “Use lowest die”; “You cannot take a dead action.”

answers.answer: Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each further Debt advance needs consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never go past the Debt track end. Chairman then allocates all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting borrowing limits. Existing office cash stays there.
answers.evidence: Actions → Chairman: “add up to three Debt freely”; “Each additional advance requires consent”; “allocate all Balance.”

answers.answer: Manager of Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. For £2 lease an extra ship; for £3 fit a ship from a shipyard (no owner consent); for £5 buy a Company ship only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships return at Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions → Manager of Shipping: “spend treasury until £2 or less remains”; costs and placements under that heading.

answers.answer: President declares home region plus any regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Treasury buys dice at £1 each; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failure may retry if affordable; catastrophe removes President. Success is limited to one Trade per President per turn. Capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone. First writer goes to home port; each later order extends the route filled during this same Trade. Other Presidency’s writers cannot extend it; writers do not limit capacity, so use available writers then filled tokens for remaining ships. No filling another President’s home region. Each order adds its printed revenue to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; President gets £1/order and writer owners £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency operations and Trade: “one successful Trade”; “one order per ship”; “Writers do not limit capacity”; “No President may fill another President’s home region.”

answers.answer: A Commander may target its Presidency’s home region, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home region or another Presidency’s Company region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice; subtract target strength plus all other regions in its empire, counting target once (Company defense strength is zero). After every attempt, roll one die for each exhausted officer; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments have no loss rolls. Noncatastrophic failures can retry with remaining resources.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: target rules, dice/penalty, and “After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted.”

answers.answer: On success take loot of £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, at least surviving officers used in the attempt plus one for Commander; distribute repeated £1 cycles: Commander first (£1 plus £1 per own used surviving officer), other families clockwise (£1 per their used surviving officer), bank last (£1 per used regiment and each alliance piece). Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome and any capital’s matching empire flags, open all its orders, clear unrest, and for new conquest put token symbol-side up above its President’s box, Governor overlay in region and Governor card only in Vacant Offices. Move Elephant inside if it faced outward. Catastrophe returns half Commander-family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; exhausted officers still roll losses; no card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: “On success, take loot”; “After loot and trophies, impose successful control”; catastrophe paragraph.

answers.answer: Governor takes its printed dice pool; each attempt rolls current pool without penalty then reduces it by one regardless of result. Success pays £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll failed, and permits exactly one success option: build one ship stage (first success places partial ship in region, later success completes it into associated sea zone), commission regiment into associated Army, or add unsplit £2 to Balance or President treasury. Tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Every unsuccessful roll adds regional unrest; catastrophe also removes Governor. Repeat with shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice, or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governors: “reduces the pool by one regardless of result”; success payout/options; tax and stop conditions.

answers.answer: Expenses are £1 per existing Debt, Army officer/regiment, and ship in sea zones including China, excluding Commanders. If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans and advance Debt one per loan until track end; loans continue even at maximum Debt. New emergency Debt adds no expense this turn; after loans set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Then Chairman may pay affordable dividends (one cash per Company share; £1/share to each holder including Chairman); if total dividends are strictly greater than expectations, Standing rises one.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Revenue: Expenses, Expectations, Dividends.

answers.answer: A normal Crisis against Company first resolves its primary attack, then secondary Rebellions in other unrestful Company regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; each Presidency Commander chooses order among its associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength is ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus target unrest; secondary strength is only that region’s unrest. Company Commander must exhaust Army pieces totaling attack strength or as much as possible; alliances count printed strength and cannot split. Defense succeeds if newly exhausted pieces equal strength; matched defense clears all target unrest and earns Commander one trophy. If it defeats a normal primary Invasion, remove one attacker tower if possible. If strength-2 alliance defends strength-1 attack, the summary explicitly says the available primary material does not settle whether it succeeds/how excess is counted. Vacant Commander is replaced for defense by Military Affairs, or Chairman if vacant, with no trophy gain/loss.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Attacks on Company and FAQ: “primary Crisis first”; “secondary regions in Bombay → Madras → Bengal”; “treatment of an indivisible alliance exceeding the required strength is unresolved.”

answers.answer: PM draws at least one law. After one or two ordinary draws, may stop or draw up to three total, then chooses any revealed law and discards others. Drawing a dilemma forces that dilemma and ends drawing. Before voting, move dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy matching law’s bottom icon; it sets target and consequence. Voting support -1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma failure text, Opposition Leader takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one adjacent space and resolves it. Support zero or more passes: law joins passed laws, PM takes token, selected policy resolves before immediate law effects. Restore used vote cards afterward. A law causing Company failure finishes voting before scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → “After one or two ordinary…draws”; “Resolution”; effects order.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must if either is starred. Use ordinary voting/support threshold with exceptions: no policy accompanies it, PM may vote against, failure neither removes PM nor discards law. Passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM passed-law token and activates firms. Failure increases Company share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token, maximum ±3. 1813 starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: “may call…if…lined”; “must if…starred”; pass/fail outcomes; “1813 begins deregulated.”

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player managing none contributes one eligible Company share or flips a workshop to invested, flips family board to charter, places a family member as first share, sets Value to leftmost space, and takes £5 from bank into London. Further investment, with manager consent, similarly contributes a Company share/workshop and receives £5 from bank into London. Up to ten firm shares; investments above cap still add £5 but no share. Chairman share cannot be used; no Company shares when Standing or Debt is lined; shares made this turn cannot be used even after trade. Invested workshops never revert and give neither bonus nor Company-failure VP.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: investments: form, invest, and restrictions.

answers.answer: Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and must have a ship to choose trade strategy. Select strategy secretly and simultaneously; commit bid from London. Reveal bids simultaneously; matching strategies reveal and roll at start of associated Presidency, paying bid to bank; one or more 1/2 succeeds. Initiative is ships minus successful dice. President’s successful trade creates comparable initiative; after that trade, lowest initiative fills first, with President breaking ties. If President vacant or never succeeds, firms fill after Commander/Governors, with Chairman breaking ties. Fill open orders up to ships+1, starting at home port and extending only own filled route; home port must be open when filled. Each order once per firm, but can refill others’ orders and vice versa. Previously filled this turn order earns half revenue rounded down. Advance Value one per full £6 added to India treasury.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm strategies and competing trade: selection, checks, initiative, capacity, repeat fills and value.

answers.answer: At Revenue firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or Value, from either/both treasuries. If short, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, charter flips to family side; invested workshops remain invested. Rescue by emergency investment under normal contribution rules (even at ten shares; pay expenses, lose leftover cash, lower Value one per investment) or emergency merger with one other firm; normal merger consent applies and other firm first pays its own expenses, then covers endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. After expenses, manager may pay dividends from India only: £1 per share and £1 manager; shareholder may waive only with manager consent. Record actual total cash paid on Company Balance track. Active non-Hobnob firm with no payment records zero; Hobnob keeps prior marker. Sweep remaining India cash to London.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm expenses, rescue and dividends.

answers.answer: Supply is limited except Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks, which are unlimited. If a limited supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. All information including discards and family cash is public, except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.
answers.evidence: Components → Limits: “when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible”; public-information sentence.

answers.answer: The summary says firm shares can be traded like Company shares, and blackmail can be traded only before it is used: once used it is faceup and can no longer be traded. It does not give the complete list of negotiation-tradable and prohibited item types or the detailed representation procedure for a transferred Company share, so those parts are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Overview/Components: public information exception; London Season: “once used…can no longer be traded”; Deregulation: “firm shares can be traded like Company shares.”

answers.answer: The summary permits immediate and future agreements as promises, but says once the game is over negotiations and calling promises stop, and during all Final Scoring no negotiations or promise calls are allowed. It does not specify the binding status of immediate/future deals, limits or timing for calling promises, simultaneous unfulfillable calls, or repeated activation after transfer; those details are unsupported by this summary.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail”; “During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.”

answers.answer: For five players add three extra setup cards; for six add six, then shuffle and deal evenly. Each player takes listed cash, enterprises and positions; distribute holdings per placement table (e.g. offices include matching office card, shares put member in Court, ships placed in listed zone or shipyard if unfitted). Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Deal three cards for London display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup: step 3 and placement table; “Each starting luxury gives 2 VP”; step 4 London display.

answers.answer: Game ends after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is immediate, except if during Events finish that phase; legislation-caused failure finishes the vote. Final Scoring bars negotiations and promise calls, so promises or negotiations cannot continue then.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “failure during Events finishes that phase”; “legislation failure finishes vote”; “During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls.”

answers.answer: Final Power is current track power from enterprises/shares (bottom two positions zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power including faceup/down blackmail and applicable spouse. Awards are 3/1 VP for turns 1–3, 5/2 for 4–6, 8/4 for 7–8. Tied first each get only lower award; no other award. Tied second get none. The specific final-victory tie-break sequence is not stated in this summary.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Power award: sources, award schedule, tie handling.

answers.answer: If Company survives, add current Court VP per Company share. If it fails, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop; invested workshops do not receive this failure VP. At start of Final Scoring, firm shareholders may make one eligible special retirement whether Company survives or fails. After that, surviving Company uses final attrition then pensioner retirements; failed Company instead draws one random Company failure card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Court/workshops and survival/failure; firm retirement before either branch.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately when spouse is taken. Retirement discounts can stack and are personal; each discount is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: London Season: “Spouses usually add VP…” and “Retirement discounts can stack…each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.”

answers.answer: If shipyard is returned by Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. The shipyard cannot be bought while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after that ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season: Returned shipyard rule.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer: no stated cost; place writer in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices place one additional writer once that turn. Enlist Officer: no stated cost; place member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury: £4 to bank; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and window icon; social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard: £2 to bank; gain shipyard and matching ship unfitted on it; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop: £5 to bank; gain workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus; 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share: pay bank based on empty Stock Exchange space, queue £2, £3, £3, £4, £5; applicant only, not yet share.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family: Family action table and New Company shares.

answers.answer: If a family must place a piece and has none in supply, take one from any of its prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too. If no Family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family: piece reuse and no-action rule.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman; place a family member from supply, or if needed a prize member (losing that prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Hiring → Chairman election: “If Court is empty…”

answers.answer: Chairman hires Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices vacant; Manager of Shipping from any writer; Military Affairs from a Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any trainee. Director hires President from writers or associated Governor; President hires Governor from a writer or officer in region (Commander is ineligible). Chairman hires China Superintendent from any writer immediately when China is created. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way.
answers.evidence: Hiring table: office hirers and candidates; Governor General row.

answers.answer: Successful Special Envoy checks can open one closed order in a non-Company region or open China (place Superintendent overlay/card and Chairman immediately hires a writer). Director may make repeated envoy checks. After all envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones including China if created. Transfers cannot occur before envoys finish.
answers.evidence: Actions → Director of Trade: envoy effects and “After all envoys…up to two transfers.”

answers.answer: Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers of an officer or regiment between Armies, remaining in top half; next assign every trainee to any Army top half; finally appoint Commanders. Appoint if vacant or a family has more total pieces in Army than current Commander’s family, selecting among most-piece families. Move selected officer to Commander slot and incumbent back as top-half officer. A tie with incumbent does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions → Military Affairs: ordered procedure and appointment rules.

answers.answer: President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; Commander/Governors may decline. Each position completes all actions before next, and Trade can occur before/after but not interrupt another position. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only; cannot trade or approve local alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency operations and Trade: ordering and vacancy rules.

answers.answer: Trade ships do not exhaust. On nonfinal Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency Writers box, using dividers to retain affiliation; filled tokens and dividers return to supply.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh: writers, tokens/dividers, fitted ships; Trade: “Trade does not exhaust ships.”

answers.answer: At start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, request Presidency treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Purchased alliances enter active/top half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust whole alliance to bottom; printed strength is used once that turn and cannot be split between purposes. Unused active alliances exhaust at Refresh and never reactivate like officers/regiments.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: alliance purchase/exhaustion rules; Refresh rule.

answers.answer: Deploy in own Company region to reopen orders or clear unrest has zero Company defense penalty; with no tower, trophies are zero. With neither tower nor faceup loot modifier, loot is the minimum: surviving participating officers plus one for Commander, distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: “Deploying in an already Company-controlled region…”

answers.answer: A Governor needs two successful Build ship choices: first success places partial ship in Governor’s region; a later success completes it into sea zone associated with Governor’s President. Governor-commissioned regiments go into the Army associated with that President; their loot is paid to bank and they do not roll officer losses.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governors: Build Company ship stages and Commission regiment.

answers.answer: China is created by successful Director envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash; Shipping/Director may send ships there. It acts after Bengal; its ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.
answers.evidence: Actions → Superintendent of Trade in China: creation, treasury, turn timing, ship zone.

answers.answer: China may not retry: it gets only one attempt including a failed one. It must not attempt without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. Roll one die per ship. On success count export icons only in Company-controlled regions; Company Balance gets £4 per icon, Superintendent’s family gets £1 per icon from bank.
answers.evidence: Actions → Superintendent of Trade in China: one attempt, prerequisite, dice and payout table.

answers.answer: When Governor General law passes, all Governors become pensioners, overlays and partial ships are removed, Governor/Director cards go to box, and Director is replaced by Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and using Director treasury/turn slot. No new Governors/overlays on conquest; printed Company symbols show control. On region loss, skip Governor Elimination.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governor General: law effects and later conquest/loss rules.

answers.answer: Before any Govern checks, Balance gets £3 per Company region. Govern attempts cost £1 treasury per die, no penalty; each six adds unrest to every Company region, even on success, and failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Success grants £1 per Company region and requires one choice per region: complete Company ship to any sea zone including China; regiment to any Army; or £2 to Balance/any other office treasury, adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn add unrest in different regions. Only one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governor General: opening balance, Govern effects and success limit.

answers.answer: Storms: roll once per player-owned ship in affected zone; 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue or sink if already fatigued, 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern; firm ships use their strategy zone; Hobnob firm ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Storms.

answers.answer: When an order newly closes, return its writer to owner’s supply and flip filled token to closed. If region is already fully closed, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to its orders. If any connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead; if none open, it too Cascades. One region can initiate a Cascade once per event tile, but can receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Closing orders and Cascades.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the region of the new top-stack tile, cascading if all there are closed. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that region and every bordering region. Shuffle: March Elephant, shuffle that tile into remaining draw stack, then shuffle discards and put them on top; if draw stack empty, do the March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India: event table entries Turmoil, Windfall, Shuffle.

answers.answer: Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains a tower; a dominated region instead rebels using printed explosion modifier. Move Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India: Leader entry.

answers.answer: Peace on a border opens orders connected across Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is wholly inside a region instead, open all that region’s orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.
answers.evidence: Events in India: Peace entry.

answers.answer: Non-Company Invasion succeeds only when attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier is strictly greater than defender’s whole empire strength. On success replace defender flag with attacker’s dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If attacker has no empire, use free capital/star and matching small flag; if none available, no empire/flags form. On failure attacker loses one tower. Equal strength is not enough.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Invasion Crisis.

answers.answer: Non-Company Rebellion compares only the rebelling region strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital’s strength; other empire regions do not count. It must be strictly greater to succeed. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Rebellion Crisis.

answers.answer: On region loss Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and Commander member to supply; roll once per associated Army officer and each 6 removes it. Governor card/member/fatigue return to unused stack/supplies, overlay, partial ship and unrest removed. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion strength) and proper invasion flag. Control token returns region with £ loot side down and symbol side up; future conquest has no loot modifier; region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes all orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion have already closed them. Standing loss equals regions lost so far this turn (first −1, second additional −2, etc.). Failure from this loss finishes Events phase before scoring. Other Company regions are not automatically lost; resolve attacks/defenses separately.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Region Loss: destinations, checks, loot, Standing and independent losses.

answers.answer: After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant goes to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches it goes to top-stack region. In Company region place fully inside. In dominated region point toward sovereign. In sovereign region point across shape-marked border; if neighbor already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated. If all are, use redirect-arrow shape border pointing toward empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Elephant’s March.

answers.answer: Foreign Invasion target selection: roll storm die; West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms targets each, none targets top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack strength and Company-defense procedure. On success close all orders once (Cascade if all already closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to attack roll halved rounded down. Redirect Elephant with circle shape only if it was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Unrest does not add to primary attack or resulting towers; event still uses Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks, but not normal primary Crisis’s added unrest.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Foreign Invasion and FAQ → Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: PM must reveal at least one law. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws PM may stop or continue to three total, then choose any revealed law. A dilemma forces selection of itself and ends drawing. Before voting, PM moves dial clockwise or counterclockwise to first policy space matching chosen law’s bottom icon; that policy space fixes target/consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: PM drawing and proposed policy.

answers.answer: Tax: each family pays bank £1 per target it owns; unpaid target returns to supply (including Chairman if taxed). Window tax additionally requires payment per window on enterprises and prizes, returning target enterprise/prize member if unable. Bonus is bank paying each family £1 per owned target. Power swaps target with next higher Power marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Policy table.

answers.answer: Each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. A card’s votes are usable once for the whole vote across rounds: rotate when used and restore after resolution. Starting PM clockwise, players vote; after each round PM may call another or stop, but a round with no votes ends voting.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Voting: vote cost, one-use cards, rounds and stop.

answers.answer: A supporter may later oppose; once opposed, a player cannot support later in that vote. Track opposition; largest opponent is Opposition Leader, with a tie retaining current holder. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose and count toward their opposition. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Voting: support/oppose, leader and coalition restrictions.

answers.answer: Upkeep is required on final turns too: pay each prize member’s printed amount separately; if unpaid, return that member and lose that prize’s VP. On nonfinal turns, Refresh returns writers to associated Presidency Writers boxes, filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply, reactivates exhausted officers/regiments, exhausts active local alliances, and leaves fitted player-ship fatigue as is; then advance turn. Final turn skips Refresh and goes to scoring.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh: upkeep and final-turn rule/table.

answers.answer: Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of firms owned. Actual spending after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms they own shares in; a firm with absent or zero marker cannot qualify. Discounts can support higher printed-cost prize if actual payment remains within cap. Otherwise retirement proceeds normally, including prestige eligibility. At start of Final Scoring firms score, then each shareholder gets one eligible special retirement regardless of Company outcome; no display cards then.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Special retirement; Scoring: firm retirements before Company outcome.

answers.answer: Investment £5 comes from bank into London treasury; trade proceeds go to India treasury. London pays ship acquisition/fitting, bids and may pay expenses; expenses can use either/both treasuries, dividends only India. Remaining India cash sweeps to London after dividends. Family cash cannot be gifted into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase (treasuries); Firm strategies (bids); Firm expenses, rescue and dividends.

answers.answer: Firms phase occurs after Family share creation and before Hiring. Investments occur without set order until nobody wants more; manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then firms choose strategies.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: investments.

answers.answer: A firm may fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 paid from London to bank with shipyard owner consent. Cannot fit another player’s ship without consent. It cannot acquire Company or extra ships. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paid to Shipping treasury.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: Ships.

answers.answer: Hostile takeover may be initiated only by a player managing no firm at all. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of target firm shares. Move firm’s ships, money and shares to own charter and copy both cube positions; old manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: Hostile takeover.

answers.answer: Merger requires managers’ agreement and consent of every shareholder. Highest-Value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Negotiate transfers and any shares over ten with those owners’ consent. Treat whole agreement as one binding immediate transfer. Primary’s Value/dividend track continues.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: Merger.

answers.answer: Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; it retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Firm still pays expenses. Hobnob ships are exempt from storms. The summary does not mention a separate retirement marker beyond the dividend marker.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies: Hobnob row; firm expenses: “Hobnob ships are exempt.”

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investment follows normal contribution rules even at ten shares: share cap prevents additional shares but firm still receives £5 per investment contribution, pays expenses, loses any remaining cash, and Value drops one space per emergency investment. The restriction against investing shares created this turn remains part of the normal rules.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency investments; Firms phase: Invest restrictions.

answers.answer: Emergency merger is with only one other firm, rather than the general merger of firms negotiated by managers. Normal merger procedure and every involved shareholder’s consent still apply. The other firm first pays its own expenses if not yet paid, then covers endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency negotiated merger.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution needs consent of all shareholders. Use insolvent-firm dissolution: shares to Debtor’s Prison, each −1 VP; ships return to matching shipyards; charter flips to family side. Invested workshops stay invested for rest of game and do not recover.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: Voluntary dissolution.

answers.answer: Firm score is calculated separately for each player by adding VP from all that player’s firm shares, then rounding that player’s total down once. Deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Firm shares score by Value: 1=−1, 2=0, 3–4=½, 5–7=1, 8–9=1½, 10=2 VP per share. This is separate from Company outcome; Company failure affects Company-share value and uninvested workshops, not the stated firm-share scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: firm scoring and Firm-track VP per share.
Setup → Prizes table.

answers.answer: 1710 starts turn 1 and runs through 5, with no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs turns 3–7 and deregulation can be voted in. 1813 runs 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs 1–8 with deregulation available.
answers.evidence: Setup: Scenario standard scope and Scenario figures.

answers.answer: 1710 begins with £10 expectations Standing and 0 Debt, £3 each office treasury, Royal Protection law, one regiment per Army, and no Company ships. 1758 begins £12 expectations and 3 Debt, £4 each treasury, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Setup → Scenario figures: 1710 and 1758 rows; paragraph for Bengal token.

answers.answer: 1813 begins £10 expectations/0 Debt, £3 each office treasury, Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), and Calico Acts, two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Place +2/−2 share-value token in Court; create China; place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in Presidencies; return Governor General law to box and place Governor General overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors.
answers.evidence: Setup → Scenario figures and 1813 paragraph.

answers.answer: Power awards: final turns 1–3: first 3, second 1; turns 4–6: first 5, second 2; turns 7–8: first 8, second 4. If tied for first, each tied player receives only the lower award and no other award.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Power award.

answers.answer: Initial Power positions: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. Deregulation lined spaces: Standing £4/£6/£8 and Debt 5/6/7/8; starred Standing £4 and Debt 8. Standing reset S is above £10.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Start Power positions” and “For Deregulation” sentence.

answers.answer: No. Designer ruling says Foreign Invasion unrest does not add to primary attack strength or determine resulting tower levels. Use ordinary die for attack and halve that die (round down) for towers; the event retains Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks, without normal primary Crisis unrest addition. Successful Foreign Invasion closes all target orders once; if already all closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them again.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings → Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, that check fails. Company Fraud is at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest (minimum zero), and take bank cash equal only to actual Balance reduction. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demoted Commander is eligible as officer for reappointment.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings → Applicable official errata.

answers.answer: Shared setup: Company Balance starts £5; family VP markers start at zero. Put local alliances in named Army boxes; loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario and use its card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India political map; set Turn marker on its start date and PM dial arm to matching date.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2.

answers.answer: Normal turn order: London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation vote is at very start before London Season. Skip London Season on the game’s first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: phase-order line and first-turn sentence.

answers.answer: Retirement begins with Chairman; if vacant, former Chairman starts. Then clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize, paying its printed cost and gaining printed VP. Spending is set aside until London Season ends for display order, then paid to bank. Pensioners need not retire, but unused pensioners return to supply after the display step.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: Retirements.

answers.answer: No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.
answers.evidence: Components → India terminology: “Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region…”

answers.answer: Firm share VP by Value: 1: −1; 2: 0; 3: ½; 4: ½; 5: 1; 6: 1; 7: 1; 8: 1½; 9: 1½; 10: 2. Each player totals VP across all their firm shares, then rounds down once.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Firm-track VP per share and firm scoring paragraph.
